RELATIONSHIP SCORING POLICY (bank internal)
+2  account age 3 years or more (+1 if 1-3 years, 0 if under 1 year)
+2  salary/inflow credited in at least 11 of the last 12 months (+1 if 9-10, 0 otherwise)
+2  average balance above Rs 50,000 (+1 if Rs 15,000-50,000, 0 below)
+2  previous loan fully repaid, never 30+ days late (+1 if repaid with 1-2 late months, 0 if no history)
-3  any cheque/direct-debit bounce in the last 12 months (per policy, applied once)
-4  any 90+ day delinquency on eCIB in the last 24 months
-6  any write-off or litigation flag on eCIB, ever
Decision bands: score >= 6 STRONG | 3-5 ACCEPTABLE | 0-2 THIN | below 0 POOR

Product on the shelf for proactive offers: Personal Instalment Loan: Rs 50,000-Rs 3,000,000, tenors 12/24/36/48 months, 28.3% p.a. (reducing rate), processing fee 2.0%, min income Rs 50,000
Bank policy: proactive offers only to STRONG or ACCEPTABLE relationships showing genuine cash stress; THIN gets monitoring; POOR gets no unsecured offer (secured/deposit-backed alternatives only). DBR cap 40%.

Should we proactively offer this customer a loan? Walk through the decision.

No unsecured offer. The score is -2 (POOR) driven by a cheque/DD bounce in the last 12 months, a write-off/litigation flag. The cash stress is real (16 days under Rs 5,000), which makes unsecured lending here more dangerous, not less - it would likely become another delinquency.

What we can responsibly put in front of them: deposit-backed finance against any savings, gold-backed finance if they hold gold, or a secured card with a small limit to start rebuilding the file. If the write-off is disputed, tell them the eCIB correction process through the reporting bank - a cleaned record reopens the normal shelf.

MERA CHALTA LOAN
- Asal: Rs 1,070,000, 36 mahine, 30.4% p.a. (reducing)
- Instalment: Rs 45,658/mahina
- Ab tak instalments: 13
- Aaj ka outstanding principal (bank statement ke mutabiq): Rs 788,545
- Early settlement fee: outstanding ka 4%
- Bonus haath mein hai, chaahun to abhi poora utaar dun.

Aaj loan band karne se kitna bachta hai?

<think>
Step 1: chalte rehna = Rs 45,658 x 23 baqi instalments = Rs 1,050,132.
Step 2: aaj settle karna = outstanding Rs 788,545 + 4% fee Rs 31,542 = Rs 820,087.
Step 3: bachat = Rs 1,050,132 - Rs 820,087 = +230,045 PKR.
</think>

Haan - settle karo. Aaj band karne ki cost Rs 820,087 hai jabke baqi instalments Rs 1,050,132 banti hain, yani Rs 230,045 ki bachat (4% fee nikaal kar wo aainda markup jo ab nahi dena).

Do amli baatein: tehreeri settlement quote lo jis par date likhi ho (outstanding har cycle ke saath badalta hai), aur adaigi ke baad clearance letter lo aur eCIB par facility 'closed' report hone ki tasdeeq karo - yehi closed line agli baar qarz lene par aapki file behtar karti hai.

Gold-backed facility ki size nikaalo.

<think>
Step 1: assessed value = 1.7 tola x Rs 246,000 x 21/24 purity = Rs 365,925.
Step 2: 75% LTV par max loan = Rs 274,444.
Step 3: request Rs 380,000 vs cap Rs 274,444 -> grant Rs 270,000.
Step 4: Rs 270,000 par 25.3%, 24 mahine ki instalment = Rs 14,451.
</think>

Sone ki value Rs 365,925 banti hai (1.7 tola, 21K par adjust), jo 75% LTV par zyada se zyada Rs 274,444 uthati hai.

Ye Rs 380,000 ki zaroorat se Rs 110,000 kam hai - Rs 270,000 do aur baqi ka intezam kahin aur se karne do, ya pledge mein aur sona shamil ho. Rs 270,000 par instalment: Rs 14,451/mahina, 24 mahine.

Customer ko batane wali baat: pledge facility ko secure karta hai is liye rate 25.3% hai jabke unsecured personal loan ~30%+ hota hai, manzoori bureau file par nahi atakti, aur poori adaigi par sona wapis milta hai. Imandari se batane wala risk margin call hai - sona tezi se gire to bank LTV bahal karne ke liye kuch adaigi ya mazeed pledge maang sakta hai.

Calculate the EMI and the all-in cost.

<think>
Step 1: flat markup = P x rate x years = 260,000 x 37.2% x 12/12 = Rs 96,720.
Step 2: EMI = (260,000 + 96,720) / 12 = Rs 29,727.
Step 3: total paid = Rs 29,727 x 12 = Rs 356,720; processing fee = 1.0% x 260,000 = Rs 2,600.
</think>

Instalment: Rs 29,727/month for 12 months.

- Total repaid: Rs 356,720
- Markup over the life: Rs 96,720
- Processing fee (upfront): Rs 2,600
- All-in cost above principal: Rs 99,320 One caution on flat-rate quotes: a flat rate charges markup on the full principal for the whole tenor even as you pay it down, so the effective reducing-balance rate is nearly double the sticker - compare quotes on total rupees paid, not the headline rate.

Size the gold-backed facility.

<think>
Step 1: assessed value = 14.7 tola x Rs 250,000 x 22/24 purity = Rs 3,368,750.
Step 2: max loan at 70% LTV = Rs 2,358,125.
Step 3: request Rs 2,860,000 vs cap Rs 2,358,125 -> grant Rs 2,350,000.
Step 4: instalment on Rs 2,350,000 at 22.4% over 36 months = Rs 90,235.
</think>

The gold values at Rs 3,368,750 (14.7 tola adjusted to 22K), supporting a maximum of Rs 2,358,125 at 70% LTV.

That falls Rs 510,000 short of the Rs 2,860,000 requested - grant Rs 2,350,000 and let them bridge the gap elsewhere or add more gold to the pledge. Instalment on Rs 2,350,000: Rs 90,235/month for 36 months.

Worth telling the customer: because the pledge secures the facility, this prices at 22.4% against ~30%+ for unsecured personal loans, approval does not hinge on the bureau file, and the gold comes back on full settlement. The risk to flag honestly is the margin call - if gold prices fall sharply, the bank can ask for partial prepayment or extra pledge to restore the LTV.

REQUEST

How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores 3 (ACCEPTABLE) under policy, and lending unsecured into active delinquency markers sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

- Holds household gold they could pledge

How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores -1 (POOR) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Deposit-backed finance against the Rs 190,000 term deposit - up to ~90% of it at a far lower rate, approval independent of the eCIB flags since the deposit secures it
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores -3 (POOR) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores -4 (POOR) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Deposit-backed finance against the Rs 420,000 term deposit - up to ~90% of it at a far lower rate, approval independent of the eCIB flags since the deposit secures it
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

REQUEST

- Holds household gold they could pledge
- Holds a Rs 240,000 term deposit with us


How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores -4 (POOR) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Deposit-backed finance against the Rs 240,000 term deposit - up to ~90% of it at a far lower rate, approval independent of the eCIB flags since the deposit secures it
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

How do we say no here without abandoning the customer?

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores -4 (POOR) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Deposit-backed finance against the Rs 500,000 term deposit - up to ~90% of it at a far lower rate, approval independent of the eCIB flags since the deposit secures it
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

We can't approve this unsecured. Draft the decline - but with real alternatives, not a brush-off.

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores -10 (POOR) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Deposit-backed finance against the Rs 380,000 term deposit - up to ~90% of it at a far lower rate, approval independent of the eCIB flags since the deposit secures it
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

We can't approve this unsecured. Draft the decline - but with real alternatives, not a brush-off.

Decline the unsecured request - the file scores 1 (THIN) under policy, and lending unsecured into a write-off history sets the customer up for another default, not relief.

But the answer is a redirect, not a door: 
- Gold-backed finance - pledged gold typically supports 70-80% of assessed value; the collateral, not the bureau record, carries the approval
- A secured card or small nano facility repaid on time for 6-12 months, to put fresh positive lines on eCIB
- If the write-off is disputed or since settled, pursue correction/settlement letters through the reporting bank - a cleaned or 'settled' status reopens normal products

Say it plainly in the letter: what blocked approval, that it is repairable, and which of the above we will open today. A declined customer who leaves with a workable path stays a customer.

Which is actually cheapest? The rates confuse me because the types differ.

- Offer A: flat markup Rs 156,600, EMI Rs 109,717 -> total Rs 1,316,600 + fee Rs 34,800 = Rs 1,351,400

The trap to avoid: a flat rate applies markup to the full Rs 1,160,000 for all 12 months even as the balance falls, so a 13.5% flat sticker is roughly double that in reducing-balance terms. Total rupees is the only fair comparison.
